subject: regression with measurement error / uncertainty on both x and y values

messages.author: d42c7062482960a4
messages.subject: regression with measurement error / uncertainty on both x and y values
parts:
I'd like to fit a simple regression model (y ~ x+z), but have uncertainty (sd) on both the x-values and the y-values. Is there any way to do this in INLA?
I found the model that deals with measurement error on y: https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/latent/meb.pdf

Thanks

Roel

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] regression with measurement error / uncertainty on both x and y values
parts:
yes, these measurement error models is what is available.

you cn also check the paper in series-C

@Article{art561,
author = {S. Muff and A. Riebler and H. Rue and P. Saner and L.
Held},
title = {Bayesian analysis of measurement error models using
integrated nested {L}aplace approximations},
journal = JRSSC,
keywords = {year2015,my.own,my.cv},
year = 2015,
volume = 64,
number = 2,
pages = {231--252}

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] regression with measurement error / uncertainty on both x and y values
parts:
Sorry, but my collaborator and I were not able to find such models in the paper you referred to: the 3 examples all only contain measurement error on the x-values.

We're looking for something that would in brms would be coded like this
D_obs | mi(D_sd) ~ 1 + A + me(M_obs, M_sd),
prior = c(prior(normal(0, 0.2), class = Intercept),
prior(normal(0, 0.5), class = b),
prior(normal(0, 1), class = meanme)

but we'd rather use INLA because that's what we use for the other analyses

can anyone please help?

Roel van Klink

then you set the log(precision)=0 and mark it as fixed.
